title: NorthQuay Diagnostics - integration call scrapbook
content:
High-level: quick capture from intake + technical call with NorthQuay Diagnostics (NQ). They are a small chain of urgent-care labs + teletriage for rural clinics. Main ask: embed an assistant to intake symptoms and triage red flags; must handle PHI, run in VPC/private deployment, and keep latency low enough for clinician workflow (not consumer chat).

Call summary (2025-02-11):
- Attendees: Sophie (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood Solutions Eng), Priya (Redwood Security PM), Dr. Alan Mercer (NQ CTO), Lina Osei (NQ Ops), Tom Hwang (NQ Dev).
- Use case: asynchronous collection of symptom data from patients (web + mobile) that feeds triage scoring + suggested next-step routing. Also internal clinician assistant to summarize incoming notes to reduce charting time.
- Constraints: PHI (HIPAA), KMS/HSM for keys, audit logs for every request and answer, data residency (US-East only for now), air-gapped for large hospital partner later.
- Traffic expectations: pilot ~500 requests/day across 10 clinics -> projected steady state 8k/day if rolled to 100 clinics over 6 months. Burst windows: morning check-ins could spike to ~200 req/min.
- Latency target: p95 <= 600ms for short 32-token responses when used by clinicians; for patient intake flows p95 <= 1.2s is tolerated.
- Model quality: must reliably flag red-flag symptoms with recall >= 98% on our seed eval set and hallucination rate low for medication/diagnosis recommendations (we'll measure).

Tech notes / gotchas observed:
- PHI handling: NQ wants redact-at-ingest for logs and optional full-text encrypted storage. Need transparent field-level masking suggestion. Our Private deploy supports envelope encryption but confirm audit log retention / who can decrypt.
- VPC peering: NQ network team wants to avoid NAT and prefers dedicated peering; confirm support for cross-account peering + IP allowlists.
- KMS: they use AWS KMS + in-house HSM. Need to validate KMS provider plugin for Redwood Private and key rotation flow (rotation without dropping running connections).
- Offline / flaky connectivity: many clinic sites have intermittent cellular. Design: local browser/mobile UX should queue inputs and retry; server-side we need idempotency keys and dedup detection. Note: KV cache prefixing across reconnects caused duplicate prompt context in earlier field tests. Add sticky-session note.
- Tokenization issues: clinical abbreviations (e.g., SOB = shortness of breath vs. south of boundary in notes) cause label noise. Suggest small pre-processing pass to expand/normalize common abbreviations before sending to model.
- Long past-med history: some records include multi-paragraph histories; we must avoid prompt truncation that loses the most recent encounter. Consider prefixing with chronological summary + pinned red-flag tokens (structured extractor).
- Units normalization: mmHg, mg/dL, etc. Models sometimes convert units incorrectly when asked to summarize; add unit-normalizer step in pipeline.

Initial model/infra plan (brainstorm):
- Private deployment in their AWS account (us-east-1) behind VPC; use a minimal 3-node dedicated pool for pilot (1 active + 2 standby for quick failover).
- Start with a medically-tuned LLM variant: med-moderate-v1-8q (CPU/GPU mix) — but benchmark accuracy vs hallucination. Keep ability to route to a smaller cheaper model for non-critical summarization tasks.
- Prefix caching: cache patient static context (age, meds, allergies) and only send delta to model each request. Helps latency + cost.
- Canary policy: rollout to 2 clinics first with 5 min traffic mirroring; automatic fallback to template-based triage if model confidence < threshold.

Evaluation ideas / metrics to collect:
- Red-flag recall (primary), precision (secondary), hallucination incidents (alerts when model asserts a diagnosis not present in source), de-identified leakage checks.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by route (patient-intake, clinician-summary).
- Token cost per session, tokens per patient profile, percent of requests hitting cache.
- Failure modes: number of fallbacks per day, repeat idempotency collisions.

Sample prompts (to iterate quickly):
1) Intake extraction: "You are a clinical data extractor. Patient report: <raw_text>. Return JSON with fields: main_complaint, onset_days, severity_0to10, red_flags (list), suggested_route (home/urgent/ER), confidence_score. Only emit JSON." 
2) Clinician summarize: "Summarize the below clinic note into a one-paragraph assessment and 3 bullet next-steps. Keep to facts from the note. If diagnosis uncertain, say "possible" and list supporting facts."

Notes-to-self / questions to get answers before POC:
- Confirm Redwood Private's audit log format and whether we can push logs into NQ Splunk instance. (Priya to check)
- Validate HSM/KMS integration story and key rotation process. (Marco to validate with infra team)
- Run quick token-cost calc for med-moderate-v1: projected cost for 1k sessions/day with average 350 tokens/session. (Sophie)
- Create small eval set of 200 clinic vignettes (NQ to supply 50 seed, we to augment) for red-flag recall measurement. (Tom + Sophie)

Action items (owner / due):
- Security precheck doc for NQ (draft): Priya, due 2025-02-20
- Network peering checklist and IP plan: Marco, due 2025-02-17
- Prototype prompt harness + 20 quick tests (local): Sophie, due 2025-02-14
- Jira ticket with PII masking requirements + example sensitive fields: Tom (NQ), due 2025-02-16
- Small eval vignettes: NQ ops (Lina) to drop 50 seed cases to JIRA-NQ-1287 by 2025-02-13

Risks / open concerns:
- If model hallucination on diagnosis remains >2% in test, clinicians will lose trust quickly; need hybrid rule-based guardrails first.
- Cost profile if we can't get effective prefix caching will be higher than NQ's budget; propose dedicated committed nodes for cost predictability.
- Offline UX expectations unclear — need product to define: do clinics accept delayed triage?

Misc scribbles / brainstorm (not client-ready):
- Could precompute a tiny symptom->redflag classifier (lightweight, deterministic rules) to run client-side for immediate triage and only send higher-risk cases to Redwood inference.
- Consider small fine-tune / retrieval augmentation using NQ de-identified past notes to reduce hallucination. But long-term legal review required.

Next call: schedule POC kickoff with infra + security (aim 2025-02-21). Prep: short doc with integration boundaries + sample vignettes attached.

End of notes.

Quick edit log: 2025-02-12 added action items, 2025-02-14 prompt tweaks, 2025-02-18 cleaned for internal handover to product.
